newsitem.title: ITALY: Banco Napoli cap raise 1.1 pct subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Banco Napoli cap raise 1.1 pct subscribed.

text.p: Shareholders subscribed for just 1.14 percent of Banco di Napoli's 2.0 trillion lire capital increase, opening the way for the Treasury to take control of the company.

Loss-making Banco di Napoli said in a statement on Thursday that investors had taken just 22.79 million ordinary shares in the capital increase, which closed on October 8, from the two billion shares on offer.
The Treasury has already said it would underwrite the operation and had expected to take almost all the troubled bank's stock in the wake of the cash call.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said earlier this week that the government planned to sell 60 percent of the bank by the end of the year and invited interested parties to place bids by December 20.
A Treasury official said the government would not sink cash into the company until it had seen what sort of response the sale was getting.
Banco di Napoli unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995 and plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year.
The capital increase was launched as part of a salvage operation for the debt ladden bank. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
